papers.full_text: 100 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Lilian Verduguez-Orellana1a, Aleida Verduguez-Orellana1,2b Clinical features and immunological events of cardiopulmonary syndrome caused by South American Hantavirus variants: a systematic review Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática DOI: https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 Check for updates En Bolivia circulan las variantes ANDV, RIOMV y LNV, cuya severidad clínica difiere. Objetivo: Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS) y su relación con la gravedad de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos: Revisión sistemática según la declaración PRISMA 2020. Resultados: El virus infecta el endotelio sin daño citopático directo. ANDV evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral; RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos con perfil Th1/Th17; mientras que LNV induce una respuesta equilibrada con oportuna síntesis de interferón tipo I. Estas vías alteran la permeabilidad capilar pulmonar y cardíaca, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusión: El HCPS está mediado por la respuesta inmune y su severidad depende de la variante viral. El daño tisular deriva de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y tormenta de citocinas, por lo que comprender esta inmunopatogenia es esencial para diseñar terapias dirigidas, ya que, no se cuenta con un tratamiento específico. Palabras claves: choque cardiogénico, infecciones por hantavirus, síndrome de dificultad respiratoria del adulto, síndrome pulmonar por hantavirus, tormenta de citocinas. Resumen In Bolivia, the ANDV, RIOMV, and LNV variants circulate, differing in clinical severity. Objective: To analyze the immunopathogenic mechanisms of Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and their relationship with the severity of South American variants. Methods: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: The virus infects the endothelium without direct cytopathic damage. ANDV evades the innate response, accumulating a high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile; whereas LNV induces a balanced response with timely type I interferon synthesis. These pathways alter pulmonary and cardiac capillary permeability, causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock. Conclusion: HCPS is immune-mediated, and its severity depends on the viral variant. Tissue damage stems from an uncontrolled immune response and cytokine storm; thus, understanding this immunopathogenesis is essential to design targeted therapies, as no specific treatment is available. Keywords: cardiogenic shock, hantavirus infections, adult respiratory distress syndrome, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, cytokine storm. Abstract 1Centro Universitario de Medicina Tropical (CUMETROP), Instituto de Investigaciones Biomédicas (IIBISMED), Facultad de Medicina, Universidad Mayor de San Simón, Cochabamba, Bolivia. 2Laboratorio de Radioinmunoensayo, Centro de Medicina Nuclear ahttps://orcid.org/0009-0006-3169-764X lilianverduguez@gmail.com bhttps://orcid.org/0000-0001-7896-9952 a.verduguez@umss.edu *Correspondencia: Aleida Verduguez Orellana Correo electrónico: a.verduguez@umss.edu Recibido el 30 de junio de 2026 Aceptado 16 de septiembre de 2026 https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 L a severidad del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS), desde la perspectiva biológica, es causado por diferentes variantes de hantavirus, que circulan en la región de las américas; siendo la más severa la variante Andes (ANDV)1, 2. En cambio otras variantes tales como Laguna Negra (LNV), Río Mamoré (RIOMV), ocasionan un HCSP entre moderado y leve con mejor pronóstico de recuperación3,4. Desde la perspectiva clínica, el HCPS, como evento, inicia posterior a un período de incubación de unas 2 semanas en promedio4. La fase febril del HCPS inicia con síntomas inespecíficos como fiebre, cefalea, mialgias/artralgias, sintomatología gastrointestinal3,5 y ausencia de sintomatología del tracto respiratorio superior6, estos, aparecerán recién en la fase sindrómica. La fase cardiopulmonar inicia de manera súbita con disnea progresiva acompañada de tos, además de hipoxia severa, la cual se evidencia con cianosis peribucal y desaturación de pulso. Al tercer día el paciente presenta taquicardia e hipotensión3,7. La mitad de los afectados, desarrollan daño renal agudo y un tercio presenta shock. Es en esta fase donde ocurren la gran parte de los decesos3, 6. Los eventos inmunológicos implicados en el desencadenamiento del HCSP independientemente de la variante de hantavirus responsable de la infección, son complejos e interdependientes, con la participación de la inmunidad innata mediante las AR01 Artículos de Revisión Review Article 101 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): células dendríticas y sus productos químicos próximas a las células endoteliales pulmonares, así como también la activación de la inmunidad adaptativa celular, principalmente de linfocitos CD8, complementadas con una desregulación de la respuesta inmune global caracterizada por una tormenta de citocinas4. El objetivo de la presente revisión es analizar los mecanismos inmunológicos que conducen al desarrollo del HCSP por la infección con las variantes de Hantavirus ANDV; RIOMV y LNV que circulan en el territorio boliviano y explicar desde esa perspectiva las manifestaciones clínicas que evidencian la presencia de este síndrome. Metodología Esta revisión sistemática se estructuró siguiendo los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA 2020 y fue registrada en la plataforma internacional PROSPERO con el código CRD420261437203. Consultamos exhaustivamente las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase y Scopus para literatura publicada hasta junio de 2026. Para sistematizar la información, aplicamos una estrategia de búsqueda combinada mediante operadores booleanos (AND, OR) que integró términos MeSH, DeCS y palabras clave en texto libre: ("Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome"[TiAb] OR "Andes virus"[TiAb] OR "Laguna Negra virus"[TiAb] OR "Rio Mamore virus"[TiAb]) AND ("Cytokine Storm"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Innate"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Cellular"[Mesh] OR "Capillary Permeability"[Mesh] OR "immunopathogenesis"[TiAb] OR "immune response"[TiAb] OR "Th1/Th17"[TiAb] OR "VEGF"[TiAb] OR "VE-cadherin"[TiAb]) AND ("South America"[Mesh] OR "Bolivia"[Mesh]). Se incluyo estudios observacionales, ensayos clínicos y modelos experimentales (in vitro e in vivo) enfocados en la inmunopatogenia de estas variantes sudamericanas y su relación con la gravedad clínica. Se excluyeron revisiones puramente narrativas, investigaciones ecológicas o mastozoológicas sin correlación biomédica y trabajos sobre hantavirus del Viejo Mundo. De los 1 585 registros iniciales, eliminamos 435 duplicados y evaluamos 1 150 mediante la lectura de título y resumen. Tras descartar 1 012 artículos irrelevantes, evaluamos el texto completo de 138 contribuciones, excluyendo 109 por deficiencias metodológicas o falta de datos inmunológicos específicos. Finalmente, seleccionamos 28 estudios de alta relevancia para la síntesis cualitativa; el flujo cuantitativo de selección se detalla en el diagrama PRISMA (Figura 1). Tanto el cribado de los registros como la valoración del riesgo de sesgo fueron ejecutados de manera independiente por dos investigadores, detallando la resolución de discrepancias mediante consenso o un tercer revisor. Para la evaluación del riesgo de sesgo, se midió la calidad de los diseños epidemiológicos mediante la Escala Newcastle- AR01 Figura 1. Diagrama de flujo PRISMA del proceso de selección. Elaboración propia. 102 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Ottawa (NOS), incluyendo trabajos con una puntuación ≥ 6 estrellas. En el caso de las investigaciones de ciencia básica, se empleó una lista de parámetros adaptada del Instituto Joanna Briggs (JBI), para constatar el control de variables en los modelos celulares y líneas endoteliales analizadas. Resultados Clínica de la infección por Hantavirus: variantes ANDV, LNV y RIOMV Los hantavirus, variantes RIOMV, LNV, ANDV (circulantes en el territorio boliviano), producen una sintomatología similar entre todos ellos, así como también con otras variantes que circulan en la región de las américas y únicamente se diferencian en cuanto a la severidad del cuadro clínico de la enfermedad que producen1,8. La infección, se inicia por la inhalación de aerosoles procedentes de las excreciones de roedores infectados por partículas virales del grupo de los hantavirus5. Posterior a un período de incubación variable de 9 a 30 días, sin ningún síntoma clínicamente identificable, posteriormente se inicia la fase prodrómica o febril, inespecífica caracterizada por la presencia de fiebre >38 oC, mialgias intensas generalmente en músculos largos, cefalea retroorbitaria y síntomas gastrointestinales como náuseas y/o vómitos y dolor abdominal, el cual suele ser muy intenso, sobre todo cuando la infección es ocasionada por la variante ANDV y puede llegar a confundirse con un cuadro de abdomen agudo y en ciertos casos se puede llegar a evidenciar petequias en región axilar y en extremidades; además son frecuentes las manifestaciones hemorrágicas como la hematuria, metrorragia o hemoptisis2,3,5,9. Durante este período, destaca la ausencia de síntomas del tracto respiratorio superior6. La etapa de transición crítica, comienza al segundo día de iniciada la sintomatología, cuando las variantes implicadas son RIOMV y LNV; en cambio recién inicia al tercer día en el caso de la variante ANDV; esta etapa comprende un período variable AR01 Clínica e inmunología del HCPS Figura 2. Patogénesis comparativa de tres variantes sudamericanas de Hantavirus a nivel del tracto respiratorio. Composición gráfica generada por IA en base a las referencias 1 a 10. Artículos de Revisión Review Article 103 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): de entre 8 a 24 horas6,9, con el comienzo evidente de la fase cardiopulmonar marcada por la aparición súbita de tos seca, disnea, inicialmente leve que progresa rápidamente a grave, y taquipnea (>22 rpm) indicando hipoxia3,8, la misma que, en casos severos, habitualmente relacionados con la infección por la variante ANDV, se manifiesta con cianosis peribucal, además de retracción intercostal y crepitantes bibalares a la auscultación pulmonar7. Al cuarto día, se evidencia taquicardia (>100 lpm) e hipotensión3,5,9. Finalmente, se instaura un edema pulmonar no cardiogénico llevando a una insuficiencia respiratoria aguda y en un 33% de los casos, independientemente de la variante de Hantavirus implicada, se produce shock cardiogénico con resistencia vascular periférica normal con insuficiencia cardíaca congestiva aguda, causando así, la mayor parte de los decesos5,6,9. Los que sobreviven a la fase crítica pasan a la fase de convalecencia que se caracteriza por diuresis elevada, resolución del edema pulmonar en las siguientes 24 a 48 horas y retiro progresivo de la oxigenoterapia. La recuperación completa puede llevar hasta dos años2,5. Existe escasa información clínica específica, respecto a la infección por la variante RIOMV, y se señala que esta variante además de lo señalado anteriormente ocasiona hemorragia intraparenquimal en los dos hemisferios y hemorragia subaracnoidea junto a un cuadro clínico hepatomegalia y daño renal agudo al segundo día7. Por el contrario, en la infección por la variante LNV se evidencia una clínica con menor severidad y mayor incidencia de infecciones leves o subclínicas, con una carga viral baja y una letalidad menor al 20%3,10. Respecto a la variante ANDV, las evidencias clínicas adicionales señalan también la afección del sistema nervioso central con encefalitis acompañada de cefalea intensa y fotofobia11 y una letalidad cercana al 40%2. Infección por Hantavirus variantes sudamericanas y Respuesta inmune Las variantes sudamericanas de hantavirus, infectan las células endoteliales del tracto respiratorio, mediante su acoplamiento a las integrinas αvβ3 y αIIbβ3, alterando el proceso de señalización celular habitual para posibilitar la replicación viral masiva, pero sin ocasionar un efecto citopático directo4,13. La variante ANDV, infecta de la forma anteriormente descrita, vía las integrinas, además de las células epiteliales de los alvéolos respiratorios también a las células de las glándulas salivales humanas1,2,3. Tras su ingreso a la células, la maquinaria viral, mediante su proteína no estructural NSs, inhibe la respuesta inmune innata, por interacción con la proteína adaptadora celular MAVS (Mitochondrial Antiviral-Signaling Protein), bloqueando la producción de los interferones tipo I; al silenciar la producción de estos interferones, la maquinaria viral permite acumular altas cargas virales intracelulares14,15,16, que posteriormente ejercerán un efecto indirecto en el desencadenamiento del HCPS17. Esta evasión inicial de la respuesta inmune innata, además impacta tardíamente en el brazo adaptativo de la respuesta inmune, caracterizado por una desmedida expansión clonal de linfocitos T CD8+ citotóxicos hiperactivados, los cuales migran masivamente al endotelio pulmonar, donde inducen AR01 Figura 3. Fisiopatología del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS). Composición gráfica generada por IA en base a las referencias 4, 24-28. 104 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): AR01 un daño tisular mediado por la acción de perforinas y citocinas proinflamatorias, desestabilizando las uniones intercelulares estrechas sin causar lisis celular directa18. A diferencia de los mecanismos disruptivos de la respuesta inmune empleados por la maquinaria viral de la variante ANDV, la variante RIOMV, una vez ingresada dentro las células endoteliales, promueve la hiperestimulación desregulada de la inmunidad innata a partir de la interacción del RNA viral con los receptores tipo Toll 3 y 7 (TLR-3/7) el RIG-I (Gen I inducible por ácido retinoico), generando una transcripción explosiva de las quimiocinas: RANTES, IP-10 y MCP-1 las cuales a su vez inducen el reclutamiento de monocitos y macrófagos alveolares de forma masiva19. Los monocitos/macrófagos, activan la enzima iNOS y liberan niveles nocivos de óxido nítrico y citocinas pirogénicas (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6)20. A nivel de la respuesta inmune adaptativa, la hiperestimulación desregulada de la respuesta innata, distorsiona el microambiente linfoide, polarizando fuertemente la diferenciación de linfocitos T colaboradores (CD4+) hacia los perfiles efectores Th1 y Th1721. Mientras que la vía Th1 perpetúa el daño celular mediante la liberación sostenida de IFN-γ, el perfil Th17 exacerba el reclutamiento de neutrófilos y desestabiliza directamente la barrera endotelial pulmonar mediante la secreción de IL-1722. Esta sinergia inmunopatológica culmina en una disfunción endotelial profunda, aumento de la permeabilidad capilar y el cuadro grave de SCPH documentado en infecciones por RIOMV3,4,7. El mecanismo empleado por la variante LNV, a diferencia de las dos anteriores, una vez que ingresa a las células endoteliales del tracto respiratorio, es el de estimular un acoplamiento simétrico y controlado entre los componentes innato y adaptativo de la respuesta inmune23. La variante LNV no suprime eficazmente las vías de señalización de los receptores de reconocimiento de patrones (PRRs), permitiendo una síntesis oportuna de IFN Tipo I en las fases iniciales, posibilitando así, la limitación de la replicación microvascular temprana, impidiendo altas cargas virales en el parénquima pulmonar10. A nivel de la respuesta inmune adaptativa, las células dendríticas maduran en un microambiente inflamatorio controlado, favoreciendo una diferenciación linfocitaria T equilibrada eficiente y una rápida maduración de la inmunidad humoral4 (Figura 2). Discusión Síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus y desregulación de la respuesta inmune Clínicamente, el HCPS se origina después de un período variable de incubación viral post infección en función de la variante de Hantavirus implicada2-9; en cambio, los eventos inmunológicos desencadenantes de este síndrome, inician en la etapa temprana de la infección, a partir de la alteración de la integridad de la barrera endotelial, con lo cual se incrementa la permeabilidad vascular, que si bien no es aun clínicamente identificable, la misma, en la etapa sindrómica se verá mucho más incrementada como resultado de la tormenta de citocinas, que se denomina retroalimentación positiva en la afección de la permeabilidad4. La alteración de la integridad de la barrera endotelial, como ya se señaló previamente, responde a la interacción de las variantes de Hantavirus con las moléculas integrinas β3, presentes en las células endoteliales, esta interacción, produce la hipersensibilidad de las células endoteliales el VEGF (Factor de Crecimiento Endotelial Vascular, por sus siglas en inglés) y una inhibición de la capacidad de migración de las células endoteliales sobre vitronectina4,24. full_text_sections.full_text: 100 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Lilian Verduguez-Orellana1a, Aleida Verduguez-Orellana1,2b Clinical features and immunological events of cardiopulmonary syndrome caused by South American Hantavirus variants: a systematic review Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática DOI: https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 Check for updates En Bolivia circulan las variantes ANDV, RIOMV y LNV, cuya severidad clínica difiere. Objetivo: Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS) y su relación con la gravedad de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos: Revisión sistemática según la declaración PRISMA 2020. Resultados: El virus infecta el endotelio sin daño citopático directo. ANDV evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral; RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos con perfil Th1/Th17; mientras que LNV induce una respuesta equilibrada con oportuna síntesis de interferón tipo I. Estas vías alteran la permeabilidad capilar pulmonar y cardíaca, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusión: El HCPS está mediado por la respuesta inmune y su severidad depende de la variante viral. El daño tisular deriva de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y tormenta de citocinas, por lo que comprender esta inmunopatogenia es esencial para diseñar terapias dirigidas, ya que, no se cuenta con un tratamiento específico. Palabras claves: choque cardiogénico, infecciones por hantavirus, síndrome de dificultad respiratoria del adulto, síndrome pulmonar por hantavirus, tormenta de citocinas. Resumen In Bolivia, the ANDV, RIOMV, and LNV variants circulate, differing in clinical severity. Objective: To analyze the immunopathogenic mechanisms of Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and their relationship with the severity of South American variants. Methods: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: The virus infects the endothelium without direct cytopathic damage. ANDV evades the innate response, accumulating a high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile; whereas LNV induces a balanced response with timely type I interferon synthesis. These pathways alter pulmonary and cardiac capillary permeability, causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock. Conclusion: HCPS is immune-mediated, and its severity depends on the viral variant. Tissue damage stems from an uncontrolled immune response and cytokine storm; thus, understanding this immunopathogenesis is essential to design targeted therapies, as no specific treatment is available. Keywords: cardiogenic shock, hantavirus infections, adult respiratory distress syndrome, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, cytokine storm. Abstract 1Centro Universitario de Medicina Tropical (CUMETROP), Instituto de Investigaciones Biomédicas (IIBISMED), Facultad de Medicina, Universidad Mayor de San Simón, Cochabamba, Bolivia. 2Laboratorio de Radioinmunoensayo, Centro de Medicina Nuclear ahttps://orcid.org/0009-0006-3169-764X lilianverduguez@gmail.com bhttps://orcid.org/0000-0001-7896-9952 a.verduguez@umss.edu *Correspondencia: Aleida Verduguez Orellana Correo electrónico: a.verduguez@umss.edu Recibido el 30 de junio de 2026 Aceptado 16 de septiembre de 2026 https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 L a severidad del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS), desde la perspectiva biológica, es causado por diferentes variantes de hantavirus, que circulan en la región de las américas; siendo la más severa la variante Andes (ANDV)1, 2. En cambio otras variantes tales como Laguna Negra (LNV), Río Mamoré (RIOMV), ocasionan un HCSP entre moderado y leve con mejor pronóstico de recuperación3,4. Desde la perspectiva clínica, el HCPS, como evento, inicia posterior a un período de incubación de unas 2 semanas en promedio4. La fase febril del HCPS inicia con síntomas inespecíficos como fiebre, cefalea, mialgias/artralgias, sintomatología gastrointestinal3,5 y ausencia de sintomatología del tracto respiratorio superior6, estos, aparecerán recién en la fase sindrómica. La fase cardiopulmonar inicia de manera súbita con disnea progresiva acompañada de tos, además de hipoxia severa, la cual se evidencia con cianosis peribucal y desaturación de pulso. Al tercer día el paciente presenta taquicardia e hipotensión3,7. La mitad de los afectados, desarrollan daño renal agudo y un tercio presenta shock. Es en esta fase donde ocurren la gran parte de los decesos3, 6. Los eventos inmunológicos implicados en el desencadenamiento del HCSP independientemente de la variante de hantavirus responsable de la infección, son complejos e interdependientes, con la participación de la inmunidad innata mediante las AR01 Artículos de Revisión Review Article 101 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): células dendríticas y sus productos químicos próximas a las células endoteliales pulmonares, así como también la activación de la inmunidad adaptativa celular, principalmente de linfocitos CD8, complementadas con una desregulación de la respuesta inmune global caracterizada por una tormenta de citocinas4. El objetivo de la presente revisión es analizar los mecanismos inmunológicos que conducen al desarrollo del HCSP por la infección con las variantes de Hantavirus ANDV; RIOMV y LNV que circulan en el territorio boliviano y explicar desde esa perspectiva las manifestaciones clínicas que evidencian la presencia de este síndrome. Metodología Esta revisión sistemática se estructuró siguiendo los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA 2020 y fue registrada en la plataforma internacional PROSPERO con el código CRD420261437203. Consultamos exhaustivamente las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase y Scopus para literatura publicada hasta junio de 2026. Para sistematizar la información, aplicamos una estrategia de búsqueda combinada mediante operadores booleanos (AND, OR) que integró términos MeSH, DeCS y palabras clave en texto libre: ("Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome"[TiAb] OR "Andes virus"[TiAb] OR "Laguna Negra virus"[TiAb] OR "Rio Mamore virus"[TiAb]) AND ("Cytokine Storm"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Innate"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Cellular"[Mesh] OR "Capillary Permeability"[Mesh] OR "immunopathogenesis"[TiAb] OR "immune response"[TiAb] OR "Th1/Th17"[TiAb] OR "VEGF"[TiAb] OR "VE-cadherin"[TiAb]) AND ("South America"[Mesh] OR "Bolivia"[Mesh]). Se incluyo estudios observacionales, ensayos clínicos y modelos experimentales (in vitro e in vivo) enfocados en la inmunopatogenia de estas variantes sudamericanas y su relación con la gravedad clínica. Se excluyeron revisiones puramente narrativas, investigaciones ecológicas o mastozoológicas sin correlación biomédica y trabajos sobre hantavirus del Viejo Mundo. De los 1 585 registros iniciales, eliminamos 435 duplicados y evaluamos 1 150 mediante la lectura de título y resumen. Tras descartar 1 012 artículos irrelevantes, evaluamos el texto completo de 138 contribuciones, excluyendo 109 por deficiencias metodológicas o falta de datos inmunológicos específicos. Finalmente, seleccionamos 28 estudios de alta relevancia para la síntesis cualitativa; el flujo cuantitativo de selección se detalla en el diagrama PRISMA (Figura 1). analysis.methods: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, synthesizing published literature on hantavirus immunopathogenesis.
analysis.results: Variants induce HCPS by infecting endothelial cells without direct cytopathic effect; ANDV evades innate immunity and accumulates high viral load, RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile, and LNV elicits a balanced type‑I interferon response. These pathways increase pulmonary and cardiac capillary permeability, causing non‑cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock, with tissue damage driven by uncontrolled cytokine release.

papers.title_zh: 南美汉坦病毒变种导致的汉坦病毒心肺综合征的临床表现与免疫事件:系统综述

analysis_zh.background: 本研究探讨不同南美洲 汉坦病毒 变种(安第斯病毒 (ANDV)、RIOMV、LNV)如何诱发汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS),以及为何变种特异的免疫应答会影响疾病严重程度。
analysis_zh.methods: 依据 PRISMA 2020 指南进行系统综述,综合已发表的关于 汉坦病毒 免疫发病机制的文献。
analysis_zh.results: 这些变种通过感染内皮细胞(无直接细胞致病效应)诱发汉坦病毒心肺综合征;安第斯病毒 (ANDV) 逃避先天免疫并积累高病毒载量,RIOMV 过度刺激巨噬细胞产生 Th1/Th17 型应答,LNV 则诱导平衡的 I 型干扰素应答。这些通路提升肺部和心脏毛细血管通透性,导致非心源性肺水肿和心源性休克,组织损伤由失控的细胞因子释放驱动。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本综述强调,汉坦病毒心肺综合征的严重程度由免疫介导且取决于变异株,凸显在缺乏特异性抗病毒治疗时亟需针对性抗炎疗法。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未在提供的证据中报告。

papers.title: Epigenetics of HFRS: Linking Immunity, Pathogenesis, and Vaccine-Induced Protection.
papers.abstract: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Old World hantaviruses, including Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV), is an important public-health concern, particularly in Asia. Clinical manifestations range from febrile illness to vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, haemorrhage and acute kidney injury. The mechanisms underlying variation in disease severity and the variability and durability of vaccine-induced immunity remain incompletely understood. Epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin regulation and non-coding RNA-mediated regulation, can influence antiviral immunity and immune-cell function in several biological settings; however, their specific contributions to HFRS remain insufficiently characterized. This structured narrative review examines hantavirus-specific evidence alongside relevant findings from other viral infections and vaccination settings, focusing on inflammatory responses, endothelial dysfunction, regulatory non-coding RNAs, trained immunity and potential applications in vaccinology. Experimental HTNV studies and clinical investigations of regulatory RNAs have identified candidate pathways associated with hantavirus-host interactions; however, these findings do not establish that epigenetic mechanisms determine HFRS severity or clinical outcomes. Similarly, preclinical hantavirus vaccine studies and early clinical evaluations provide evidence regarding immunogenicity and safety but do not demonstrate epigenetic mediation of protective immunity. Findings from Andes virus (ANDV), associated primarily with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), and other viral systems are therefore considered comparative or contextual evidence, not directly generalizable to HFRS. This review identifies critical knowledge gaps and outlines how longitudinal, cell-resolved epigenomic profiling, functional validation and integrated multi-omics could clarify causal mechanisms, explain interindividual variation in disease outcomes and vaccine responses, and establish the potential translational value of epigenetic biomarkers and interventions.

analysis_zh.background: 在亚洲,旧世界汉坦病毒(HTNV、SEOV)引起的肾综合征出血热是重大公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述调查了汉坦病毒特异的表观遗传证据和比较性发现,重点强调炎症反应、内皮功能障碍、调控性非编码RNA、训练性免疫以及疫苗的意义。
analysis_zh.current_state: 导致疾病严重程度和疫苗诱导免疫持久性的机制尚未完全阐明,且表观遗传对HFRS的贡献尚不明确。
analysis_zh.gaps: 影响HFRS结局的特定表观遗传机制仍未得到充分表征,现有数据也未能证明因果关系。
analysis_zh.future_research: 建议开展纵向、细胞分辨的表观基因组分析、功能验证以及整合的多组学研究,以阐明因果机制、解释个体间差异,并评估表观遗传生物标志物或干预措施。

papers.title: Hantavirus RNA Detection in Small Mammals and Spatial Comparison with Reported Human HFRS Cases in West Kazakhstan Region, 2025
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease associated with orthohantaviruses maintained in natural rodent hosts. This study assessed the detection and spatial distribution of hantavirus RNA among small mammals in the West Kazakhstan Region in 2025 and compared rodent surveillance findings with human HFRS occurrence. An observational cross-sectional analytical study was conducted in July and September 2025 in four districts. A total of 343 small mammals were captured and morphologically identified. Lung tissue samples from 329 animals collected in September were examined in 123 pooled testing units, whereas 14 animals collected in July were tested individually. Thus, 137 testing units representing 343 animals were evaluated by real-time and conventional RT-PCR. The minimum infection rate (MIR) was calculated as a descriptive minimum estimate, and a pooled-testing likelihood model was used to account for variation in testing-unit size. Hantavirus RNA was detected in 47/137 testing units, including 45 positive pooled units and two individually positive specimens. Based on 343 individual animals, the descriptive MIR was 13.7%. The model-based individual-level infection probability was estimated at 18.0% (95% profile-likelihood CI: 13.5–23.1%). Positive testing units were observed among the Ural field mouse (Apodemus uralensis), bank vole (Myodes glareolus), and common vole (Microtus arvalis). At the district level, the descriptive MIR ranged from 11.6% in Burlinsky to 19.0% in Chingirlauisky. Sampling sites overlapped spatially with settlements reporting human HFRS cases, including Utvinka, Daryinsk, and Rubezhinskoye; however, spatial coincidence does not establish direct transmission.

Limitations: Abstract‑only data; spatial overlap does not prove transmission; cross‑sectional design limits causality.

analysis_zh.methods: 在2025年7月和9月于四个区开展了观察性横断面分析研究,捕获了343只小型哺乳动物;对329只动物的肺组织在123个合并样本和14只单独动物中使用实时和常规RT-PCR进行检测,计算最低感染率(MIR),并应用合并检测似然模型。

analysis_zh.limitations: 仅有摘要数据可用,空间重合并不直接证明传播;横断面设计限制了因果推断。

papers.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells 1 . However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms-occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus-receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

papers.title: An ONT sequencing framework for hantavirus genome assembly, variant analysis, and defective viral genome characterization from whole-segment amplicons
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease. Whole genome sequencing remains difficult because of low viral loads, high sequence diversity, and an inherent instability of the viral L segment. Current tiled amplicon and hybrid-capture approaches do not capture the heterogeneity of virus populations, including defective viral genomes (DVGs), which have never been described for hantaviruses. Here, we present an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework based on universal reverse transcription primers targeting the conserved genome termini of orthohantaviruses and a single species-specific primer pair per segment, enabling amplification and sequencing of complete S, M, and L segments. We also developed an accompanying bioinformatic pipeline that performs reference-guided assembly of hantavirus genomes, consensus generation, variant calling, and DVG classification using the newly developed ORCHID classification pipeline. We applied this approach to diverse Puumala virus strains from infected cell cultures and bank voles, to representative Old World and New World orthohantaviruses, and to highly pathogenic New World viruses in vivo. In all cases we were able to accurately reconstruct full hantavirus genomes. Notably, we found that hantavirus populations contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L segment deletions, whereas the S and M segments remained largely intact. Together, this work provides a low-cost, broadly applicable and easily customisable workflow for hantavirus genomics and reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations. IMPORTANCE Hantaviruses cause severe and often fatal human diseases, and their diversity and low viral loads make them hard to sequence, which limits surveillance and outbreak investigation. We describe a simple, universal but customisable, low-cost nanopore sequencing workflow that recovers complete genome segments, including the full-length L segment, from cell culture and animal tissues across the entire Orthohantavirus genus. Using this approach, we report the first evidence of defective viral genomes in hantaviruses. These truncated genomes arise mainly from the L segment, which encodes the viral polymerase, and are formed at conserved genomic regions. Defective viral genomes can modulate viral replication, innate immune activation, and persistence in other viruses. Their presence in hantaviruses raises new questions about polymerase function, tolerance in reservoir hosts, and immune-mediated disease in humans. Our framework offers a practical tool for hantavirus genomics and a foundation for investigating how defective genomes shape hantavirus infection.

analysis.background: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic, tri‑segmented negative‑sense RNA viruses of rodents and other small mammals that can cause severe human disease (A1).
analysis.methods: The authors developed an Oxford Nanopore Technologies sequencing framework using universal reverse‑transcription primers targeting conserved genome termini and a single species‑specific primer pair per segment, coupled with a reference‑guided bioinformatic pipeline for assembly, consensus generation, variant calling, and defective viral genome (DVG) classification (A4, A5).
analysis.results: Full S, M, and L segment genomes were accurately reconstructed from diverse samples (A7); hantavirus populations were found to contain highly abundant DVGs and conserved L‑segment deletions, while S and M segments remained largely intact (A8, A12, A13).
analysis.contribution: The workflow provides a low‑cost, broadly applicable tool for hantavirus genomics across the genus, enabling surveillance and outbreak investigation, and it reveals DVGs as a previously unrecognized feature of hantavirus populations (A9, A10, A11, A16).
analysis.limitations: Only the abstract is provided, so detailed experimental design, sample sizes, quantitative metrics, and validation data are not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Orthohantaviruses are zoonotic RNA viruses causing severe human disease (A1). Methods: An ONT sequencing framework with universal primers and a custom bioinformatic pipeline was created for full‑segment amplification and analysis (A4, A5). Results: Complete genomes were reconstructed and abundant L‑segment defective viral genomes were identified (A7, A8, A12, A13). Contribution: The low‑cost workflow enhances hantavirus surveillance and reveals DVGs as a novel population feature (A9, A10, A11, A16). Limitations: Only the abstract is available, so detailed methods, sample sizes, and quantitative results are not reported.

analysis_zh.background: 正汉坦病毒es 是一种来源于啮齿动物及其他小型哺乳动物的动物源性、三段负链RNA病毒,可导致严重的人类疾病 (A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者开发了一套 Oxford Nanopore Technologies 测序框架,使用针对保守基因组末端的通用逆转录引物以及每个片段的单一物种特异性引物对,并结合参考引导的生物信息学流程进行组装、共识生成、变异检测和缺陷病毒基因组(DVG)分类 (A4, A5)。
analysis_zh.results: 从多种样本中准确重建了完整的 S、M、L 片段基因组 (A7);汉坦病毒 群体中发现大量 DVG 以及保守的 L 片段缺失,而 S 和 M 片段基本保持完整 (A8, A12, A13)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 该工作流程提供了一种低成本、广泛适用的 汉坦病毒 基因组学工具,可用于全属的监测和疫情调查,并揭示 DVG 是 汉坦病毒 群体中先前未被识别的特征 (A9, A10, A11, A16)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供了摘要,因而未在所提供的证据中报告详细的实验设计、样本量、定量指标和验证数据。

papers.title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial-coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet-leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

papers.title_zh: 新发和再新发RNA病毒感染中的血管程序:来自SARS-CoV-2、黄病毒和汉坦病毒的比较经验。

analysis_zh.background: 新发和再发RNA病毒常导致血管渗漏、血小板功能失调、凝血失衡、微血管损伤以及血栓炎症 (A1)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒以及汉坦病毒es为互补模型,阐明四个相互重叠的血管程序——内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍 (A2)。
analysis_zh.current_state: 一个共享的内皮‐凝血框架将临床、病理和实验证据综合为这四个程序 (A3)。
analysis_zh.gaps: 作者承认该框架是概念性的而非定量的,强调需要系统的分类和验证 (A4)。
analysis_zh.future_research: 他们提出构建跨病毒生物标志物面板、开发器官特异性内皮模型,并开展基于表型的临床研究以检验该框架 (A5)。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：新发和再发RNA病毒常导致血管渗漏、血小板功能失调、凝血失衡、微血管损伤以及血栓炎症 (A1)。 主要方向：本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒以及汉坦病毒es为互补模型,阐明四个相互重叠的血管程序——内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍 (… 研究现状：一个共享的内皮‐凝血框架将临床、病理和实验证据综合为这四个程序 (A3)。 不足：作者承认该框架是概念性的而非定量的,强调需要系统的分类和验证 (A4)。 后续研究：他们提出构建跨病毒生物标志物面板、开发器官特异性内皮模型,并开展基于表型的临床研究以检验该框架 (A5)。

papers.title: Can Hantavirus cruise into the next pandemic?
papers.abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.

papers.title: Vaccines Against Hantavirus Infections: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hantaviruses infections are responsible for a hemorrhagic fever with renal and cardiopulmonary syndrome with case-fatality rates up to 50%. While inactivated vaccines are already available in China and South Korea, several additional candidate vaccines are under development. This systematic review summarizes the current clinical evidence on immunogenicity and short-term safety of vaccines targeting different hantavirus strains. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic literature search was carried out to identify randomized and nonrandomized trials of any phase. Data were synthesized narratively within strata defined by vaccine platform, target virus, assay, immunogenicity and safety. Results: Ten trials on 961 adults were included: four single-arm trials on the inactivated vaccine and six early-phase DNA-vaccine trials. One month after last dose, the inactivated vaccine achieved neutralizing seropositivity by PRNT 50 in 45.1% of the tested subjects after two priming doses and 55.7% after three, while the corresponding binding-antibody values measured by IFA were 87.3% and 95.7%. Among DNA vaccines, homologous responses reached 100% against HTNV and 83.3% against PUUV with monovalent constructs, whereas dual responses to the bivalent construct were registered in 33.3% and 77.8% of the subjects, when measured through PRNT 50 and PsVNA 50 , respectively. One serious adverse event occurred, most likely unrelated to vaccination. Conclusions: No serious safety signal was identified, although safety remains insufficiently characterized. Measured immunogenicity depends as much on the assay as on the vaccine, and, in the absence of a validated correlate of protection, it cannot be read as a clinical benefit. Future research should prioritize validated correlates of protection and innovative trial designs adapted to low-incidence diseases.

analysis.background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal and cardiopulmonary syndrome and can have case‑fatality rates up to 50% (A1).
analysis.main_directions: The review examines licensed inactivated vaccines in China/South Korea and multiple DNA vaccine candidates, organized by platform, target virus, and immunogenicity assay (A2).
analysis.current_state: Ten trials involving 961 adults report modest neutralizing seropositivity for inactivated vaccines and variable DNA‑vaccine responses, with no serious safety signal detected (A3).
analysis.gaps: Immunogenicity is highly assay‑dependent, no validated correlate of protection exists, and safety data remain insufficiently characterized (A11).
analysis.future_research: Future work should establish validated correlates of protection and employ innovative trial designs appropriate for low‑incidence hantavirus disease (A12).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus infections cause severe hemorrhagic fever with up to 50% mortality (A1). Main directions: Review covers licensed inactivated vaccines and emerging DNA candidates, stratified by platform, virus, and assay (A2). Current state: Ten trials (961 adults) show modest neutralizing responses and no serious safety signals (A3). Gaps: Immunogenicity depends on assay, no protective correlate is validated, and safety remains under‑characterized (A11). Future research: Prioritize validated correlates of protection and innovative low‑incidence trial designs (A12).

papers.title_zh: 针对汉坦病毒感染的疫苗:系统文献综述。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒 感染导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,死亡率最高可达 50%(A1)。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述审查了中国/韩国已获许可的灭活疫苗以及多种DNA疫苗候选,按平台、目标病毒和免疫原性检测(A2)进行组织。
analysis_zh.current_state: 十项涉及961名成人的试验报告称,灭活疫苗的中和血清阳性率适中,DNA疫苗的应答呈变异性,未发现严重安全信号(A3)。
analysis_zh.gaps: 免疫原性高度依赖检测方法,缺乏经验证的保护相关指标,且安全性数据仍未充分表征(A11)。
analysis_zh.future_research: 未来工作应建立经验证的保护相关指标,并采用适用于低发病率 汉坦病毒 疾病的创新试验设计(A12)。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：汉坦病毒 感染导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,死亡率最高可达 50%(A1)。 主要方向：本综述审查了中国/韩国已获许可的灭活疫苗以及多种DNA疫苗候选,按平台、目标病毒和免疫原性检测(A2)进行组织。 研究现状：十项涉及961名成人的试验报告称,灭活疫苗的中和血清阳性率适中,DNA疫苗的应答呈变异性,未发现严重安全信号(A3)。 不足：免疫原性高度依赖检测方法,缺乏经验证的保护相关指标,且安全性数据仍未充分表征(A11)。 后续研究：未来工作应建立经验证的保护相关指标,并采用适用于低发病率 汉坦病毒 疾病的创新试验设计(A12)。

papers.title: Host-Virus Immune Interactions in Andes Virus Infection: Implications for Human-to-Human Transmission, Pathogenesis, and Public Health.
papers.abstract: The Andes virus (ANDV, Orthohantavirus , andesense) is unique among hantaviruses in that it may transfer from person to person and cause severe vascular damage. The evidence on host-virus immunological interactions and their importance in disease progression, transmission, and public health is compiled in this narrative review. ANDV mostly affects pulmonary endothelial cells and does not result in widespread cell loss. Rather, the loss of vascular barrier integrity is caused by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) activation, breakdown of vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin, hypoxia-related pathways, and mediators produced from infected pericytes. Additionally, the virus interferes with early antiviral defenses involving protein kinase R (PKR), TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)-interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5). The intensity or outcome of the disease has been associated with increased interleukin-6 (IL-6), altered complement activity, thrombocytopenia, neutralizing-antibody reactions, and specific host genetic variations; nevertheless, significant T-cell activation does not necessarily correspond with viral clearance. Blood and a number of mucosal and secretory samples have been found to contain ANDV ribonucleic acid (RNA), albeit RNA discovery by itself does not prove the presence of an infectious virus. Epidemiological evidence indicates that Secondary transmission is rare and mostly linked to extended close or intimate contact. Genomic sequencing, when paired with epidemiological evidence, can shed light on transmission chains. Recent outbreaks linked to travel further emphasize the significance of worldwide surveillance and coordinated contact tracing. Prospective studies integrating genomic analysis, serial virological sampling, and standardized exposure evaluation are required to more effectively define the infectious phase and transmission patterns.

Recent outbreaks linked to travel further emphasize the significance of worldwide surveillance and coordinated contact tracing. Prospective studies integrating genomic analysis, serial virological sampling, and standardized exposure evaluation are required to more effectively define the infectious phase and transmission patterns.

papers.title: Rising spillover risk: Lessons from the Andes hantavirus outbreak.
papers.abstract: The unprecedented expansion of human activity boundaries is turning spillover from a chance event into a foreseeable ecological and epidemiological certainty. Using the 2026 Andes hantavirus cruise ship outbreak as an entry point, this study examines it within a broader driver framework: nearly all emerging infectious disease events in humans in recent decades have originated from wildlife transmission; under climate-change and land-use scenarios, approximately 3139 mammal species are projected to aggregate in new combinations by 2070, causing an estimated 4000 cross-species viral transmission events. The rapid expansion of tourism into ecologically fragile regions - sub-Antarctic waters, the deep sea, and primary forests - the persistence of habitat fragmentation and animal trade, and the reshaping of wildlife distribution and vector dynamics by extreme climate events together constitute "novel contact amplifiers" that accelerate contact at the human-animal-environment interface. Robotics, artificial intelligence, autonomous driving, and automated logistics are extending human activities into previously inaccessible regions, yet they remain almost entirely absent from current spillover risk assessments. The limitations of cruise ship medical systems - whose core capacity lies in "recognize, isolate, stabilize, and transfer" rather than definitive diagnosis and treatment - were fully exposed in this event. From a One Health perspective, this paper proposes that responses to spillover risk must shift from passive reaction to proactive interface governance, incorporate technology-driven increases in contact frequency into prevention and control frameworks, and advance cornerstone strategies such as broad-spectrum vaccines and broad-spectrum antiviral drugs at the basic research level.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Expanding human activity boundaries make spillover increasingly predictable. Methods: The 2026 Andes hantavirus cruise‑ship outbreak was used as a case study within a driver framework linking wildlife transmission to emerging diseases. Results: Modeling predicts ~3,139 mammal species will form new assemblages by 2070, potentially generating ~4,000 cross‑species viral transmissions; the outbreak also revealed cruise‑ship medical system gaps. papers.title: Differential PCDH1 usage by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses associated with hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), but their cellular entry receptors have not been defined. We used replication-competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes to compare entry by these viruses, the Old World rodent-borne Dabieshan virus and Tigray virus, and the shrew-borne Cao Bang virus and Amga virus. All six Gn/Gc complexes supported infection of primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells, with virus-specific efficiencies and kinetics. Genetic ablation of protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) reduced infection mediated by Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus Gn/Gc in human osteosarcoma and endothelial cells, whereas PCDH1 re-expression restored susceptibility. Both viruses were captured by a soluble PCDH1 protein comprising the first two extracellular cadherin domains. Infection was also inhibited by a soluble decoy containing the first cadherin domain, and by an antibody specific to that domain, indicating that the first PCDH1 cadherin domain mediates viral engagement. Black Creek Canal Gn/Gc-bearing rVSVs incorporated less Gn/Gc and showed lower apparent capture by PCDH1 than Laguna Negra virus and Andes virus Gn/Gc-bearing particles, even after normalization for glycoprotein abundance. In contrast, PCDH1 depletion did not detectably alter infection mediated by the other four hantavirus Gn/Gc complexes. Thus, Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus use PCDH1 for efficient entry but differ in apparent receptor engagement and responses to PCDH1-directed inhibitors, whereas all six viruses are potently neutralized by the broadly reactive Gn/Gc-directed antibody ADI-42898. IMPORTANCE: The receptors used by many medically important hantaviruses remain incompletely characterized. Using BSL2-compatible rVSVs bearing hantavirus glycoproteins, we show that Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus, two hantaviruses associated with human cardiopulmonary disease, used protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) for efficient entry into human cells. PCDH1-directed inhibitors blocked infection, but the two viruses differed in apparent receptor engagement and inhibitor sensitivity, showing that PCDH1 usage is not uniform even among closely related viruses. Gn/Gc complexes from four additional divergent hantaviruses carried by shrews and Old World rodents infected primary human endothelial cells without detectable PCDH1 dependence, emphasizing the need to identify alternative entry factors. A broadly reactive antibody neutralized every virus in the study panel, supporting conserved viral glycoprotein surfaces as therapeutic targets when receptor usage is diverse or unknown.

analysis.background: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus are hantaviruses linked to hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), yet their cellular entry receptors have not been defined.
analysis.methods: Replication‑competent recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses (rVSVs) bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc glycoprotein complexes were used to compare entry into primary human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells and other human cell lines.
analysis.results: All six Gn/Gc complexes infected primary endothelial cells; genetic ablation of PCDH1 reduced infection by Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal viruses, which was restored by PCDH1 re‑expression; both viruses were captured by soluble PCDH1 and blocked by a decoy or domain‑specific antibody, whereas the other four viruses showed no detectable PCDH1 dependence.
analysis.contribution: The work identifies PCDH1 as a key entry factor for two HCPS‑associated hantaviruses, reveals heterogeneity in receptor engagement, and demonstrates that a broadly reactive Gn/Gc‑directed antibody can neutralize diverse hantaviruses, informing therapeutic and surveillance strategies.
analysis.limitations: Findings are derived from abstract‑only information; detailed experimental conditions, sample sizes, and in‑vivo validation are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Laguna Negra virus and Black Creek Canal virus cause HCPS but their entry receptors were unknown. Methods: Researchers used rVSVs bearing hantavirus Gn/Gc proteins to test entry into human pulmonary endothelial and other cells. Results: All six Gn/Gc complexes entered endothelial cells; PCDH1 knockout reduced entry of Laguna Negra and Black Creek Canal viruses, rescued by PCDH1 re‑expression, and both were blocked by soluble PCDH1 or a domain‑specific antibody, while the other four viruses were PCDH1‑independent. Contribution: The study defines PCDH1 as an entry factor for two HCPS viruses, shows variability in receptor use, and highlights a broadly neutralizing antibody as a therapeutic lead. Limitations: Only abstract data are available; experimental details and in‑vivo validation are missing.
